explanation: A report's specific factual claim is contradicted by a decisive observation or by a controlled repetition of the same setup. For example, the allegedly deleted value is still present, or the allegedly broken control performs the requested action when activated as described. Match this pattern only when that counterevidence addresses the same value, action and conditions; a vaguely similar successful workflow is insufficient. The finding rejects the checked allegation, not every related defect or every possible historical failure.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: In Site Administration, edit a user account. Set Maximum Number of Repositories to 0 and update the account. Reopen the edit form and check the value. The rejected report expected: The reported expectation is that a saved limit of 0 is shown as 0 when the form is reopened. It claimed this outcome: After updating a user with a maximum repository count of 0, reopening the edit form was reported to show -1. Review concluded: Not reproduced: saving 0 keeps 0. Across repeated attempts on a new user and a seeded user, typed and entered by keyboard, the request sent max_repo_creation=0 and the reopened form showed 0 every time; the server passes 0 through unchanged.

explanation: A diagnostic entry page can deliberately avoid expensive data collection until the administrator chooses a detailed view, so it remains usable when the server is under stress. In Gitea, opening Trace initially leaves the process list empty; Running Processes or Stacktrace requests and displays that information. This pattern matches calling the initial empty list a failed or broken load when those explicit views work. It does not reject the separately accepted usability defect that the initial page fails to explain how to see the traces, or an actual failure after choosing a view.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: Sign in as a site administrator. Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace. The rejected report expected: The reporter expects the Trace page to list goroutines or processes when it opens. It claimed this outcome: Opening Trace from the sidebar showed '<N> Goroutines' with no list under it. Review concluded: Intended: routers/web/admin/stacktrace.go deliberately loads no process data until Running Processes or Stacktrace is chosen ('by default, do not do anything which might cause server errors… this page is the entrance of the chance to collect diagnosis report'), so the page stays usable for downloading a diagnosis report when the server is struggling. Both tabs load the list. That the page doesn't tell the administrator how to see traces is a separate accepted bug, gitea-admin-trace-page-hides-how-to-see-traces.

explanation: A report can judge the current application using a rule that applied to an older version. Reviewed Gitea examples are assuming admin remains a reserved username after administration moved to /-/admin, and demanding a five-second profiling minimum after the supported minimum became one second. Match this mistake only when the rejection record establishes the relevant intentional version change and the observed behavior follows the current rule. A failure of the current rule or a distinct missing-feedback defect remains separate; do not reject a report merely because a feature changed historically.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Stacktrace. Enter 0, 1 or 3 in the Download diagnosis report field and download. Time the request. The rejected report expected: The reported expectation is that durations of 5 seconds or less are raised to 5 seconds. It claimed this outcome: seconds=0, empty and abc took about 1 second, seconds=3 took about 3 seconds, and seconds=10 took about 10 seconds. Review concluded: Intended: there is no 5-second minimum in this version. routers/web/admin/diagnosis.go clamps the duration to 1–300 seconds (if seconds <= 1 { seconds = 1 }); go-gitea/gitea#32973 ('Support performance trace', merged before v1.24) deliberately lowered the floor from 5 to 1, so the measured timings are the implemented behaviour. The accepted separate defect is that input below 1 second or non-numeric input is silently turned into a 1-second report with no message: 'Diagnosis report silently turns a duration below 1 second into a 1-second report'.

explanation: This benchmark is a curated evaluation with rules about which kinds of findings count. A report matches this pattern when its only established issue falls outside those rules, such as an accessibility-tree-only label problem with no accepted visible or pointer-driven failure, an invalid state reachable only through an API, or an expressly excluded exotic input. The mistake is assuming that every technical imperfection is eligible for this evaluation. Scope exclusion does not establish that the underlying issue is imaginary, and a separately demonstrated in-scope functional failure must be assessed independently.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, follow this workflow: Sign in as an administrator and open /-/admin/repos. Inspect the Op. cell's trash link in the accessibility tree. The rejected report expected: The reported expectation is that the link has an accessible name such as Delete repository <name>. It claimed this outcome: The anchor contains only an aria-hidden trash SVG with no text, title or aria-label; clicking it opens the Delete This Repository confirmation. Review concluded: Out of scope: this is screen-reader accessibility (accessible name on an icon-only link), not a functional defect. The behaviour is as described (templates/admin/repo/list.tmpl renders the link with only {{svg "octicon-trash"}}), but the icon is visible and the link opens the delete confirmation. Accessibility findings are excluded from this benchmark's ground truth.

In Gitea, follow this workflow: Sign in as an administrator and open /-/admin/config. Inspect Local Mode and Disable Router Log values in the accessibility tree. Open /-/admin/users and inspect the Activated, Restricted and 2FA cells. The rejected report expected: The reported expectation is that each value exposes accessible text such as Yes/No. It claimed this outcome: Each dd or table cell contains only an SVG with aria-hidden=true; Local Mode (check) and Disable Router Log (cross) are indistinguishable in the accessibility tree. Review concluded: Out of scope: this is screen-reader accessibility (missing text alternatives), not a functional defect. The values are rendered as described (templates/admin/config.tmpl and templates/admin/user/list.tmpl use {{svg (Iif ... "octicon-check" "octicon-x")}}), but the check and cross icons are visible and correct. Accessibility findings are excluded from this benchmark's ground truth.
